'''Dilip B. Madan''' is an American financial economist, mathematician, academic, and author. He is [[professor emeritus]] of finance at the [[University of Maryland]].<ref name=yy>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rhsmith.umd.edu/directory/dilip-b-madan|title=Dilip B. Madan &#124; Maryland Smith|website=www.rhsmith.umd.edu}}</ref>

Madan is most known for his work on the [[variance gamma model]], the [[fast Fourier transform]] method for option pricing, and the development of Conic Finance.<ref name=zx>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com.au/citations?user=fq7BQosAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Dilip B. Madan|website=scholar.google.com.au}}</ref> Madan is a recipient of the 2006 [[Humboldt Research Award]]. He has authored several books, including ''Applied Conic Finance'' and ''Nonlinear Valuation and Non-Gaussian Risks in Finance''.<ref name="auto">{{cite web|url=https://www.worldcat.org/title/1291603836|title=Nonlinear valuation and non-Gaussian risks in finance |oclc=1291603836}}</ref>

==Education==
Madan completed his [[Bachelor of Commerce]] in Accounting from the [[University of Bombay]] in 1967. In 1972, he obtained a [[Doctor of Philosophy| Ph.D.]] in Economics from the [[University of Maryland]], followed by another PhD in mathematics in 1975 from the same university.<ref name=yy/>

==Career==
Madan began his academic career in 1972 as an [[assistant professor]] of economics at the University of Maryland. In 1976, he joined the [[University of Sydney]] and held various positions, including lecturer in [[economic statistics]] from 1976 to 1979 and senior lecturer in [[econometrics]] from 1980 to 1988. Subsequently, he rejoined the University of Maryland, where he was appointed as assistant professor of finance between 1989 and 1992, served as an [[associate professor]] of finance between 1992 and 1997, and held an appointment as a professor of finance between 1997 and 2019. Currently, he is professor emeritus of finance at the University of Maryland since 2019.<ref name=yy/>

Madan has been a director and treasurer of the Scientific Association of Mathematical Finance since 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.samfinance.org/directors|title=Directors|website=SAMF}}</ref>

==Research==
Madan's [[quantitative finance]] research has won him the 2021 Northfield Financial Engineer of the Year Award from the International Association for Quantitative Finance.<ref name=aa>{{Cite web|url=https://iaqf.org/event-4771611#:~:text=2021+IAQF/Northfield+Financial+Engineer,of+the+Year+(FEOY).|title=IAQF – IAQF/Northfield Financial Engineer of the Year Award Dinner|website=iaqf.org}}</ref> He has authored numerous publications spanning the areas of [[financial markets]], [[general equilibrium theory]], and [[mathematical finance]] including books and articles in peer-reviewed journals.<ref name=zx/>

===Valuation model===
Madan's valuation model research has contributed to the improvement and development of valuation models in various fields including business and finance.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/2519144|title=Option Valuation Using the Fast Fourier Transform}}</ref> In his analysis of the impact of model risk on the valuation of barrier options, he highlighted the divergent pricing outcomes of up-and-out call options resulting from the use of different stochastic processes to calibrate the underlying vanilla options surface.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1108/eb022961|title=The Effect of Model Risk on the Valuation of Barrier Options|first1=Ali|last1=Hirsa |first2=Georges |last2=Courtadon |first3=Dilip B.|last3=Madan |date=January 1, 2003|journal=The Journal of Risk Finance|volume=4|issue=2|pages=47–55|via=Emerald Insight|doi=10.1108/eb022961|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He conducted pricing comparisons between Sato processes and conventional models, revealing that Sato processes exhibit relatively higher pricing for cliquets, while effectively preserving the value of long-dated out-of-the-money realized variance options.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/14697680701861419|title=Sato processes and the valuation of structured products|first1=Ernst|last1=Eberlein|first2=Dilip B.|last2=Madan|date=February 8, 2009|journal=Quantitative Finance|volume=9|issue=1|pages=27–42|via=CrossRef|doi=10.1080/14697680701861419|s2cid=16991478 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> Focusing his research efforts on credit value adjustments, his study proposed a theory of capital requirements to address the problem of cross-default exposures.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/14697688.2012.682607|title=From credit valuation adjustments to credit capital commitments|first=Dilip B.|last=Madan|date=June 8, 2012|journal=Quantitative Finance|volume=12|issue=6|pages=839–845|via=CrossRef|doi=10.1080/14697688.2012.682607|s2cid=154284497 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> Furthermore, he presented a Markov chain-based method for valuing structured financial products, offering financial institutions a tool to assess locally capped and floored cliquets, as well as unhedged and hedged variance swap contracts.<ref>{{cite journal
 | last1 = Madan | first1 = Dilip B.
 | last2 = Pistorius | first2 = Martijn
 | last3 = Schoutens | first3 = Wim
 | date = January 2013
 | doi = 10.1080/14697688.2011.605383
 | issue = 1
 | journal = Quantitative Finance
 | pages = 125–136
 | ssrn = 1563500
 | title = The valuation of structured products using Markov chain models
 | volume = 13}}</ref> He also introduced a conic finance-based nonlinear equity valuation model, which integrated risk charges contingent upon measure distortions.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s11579-018-0219-2|title=Nonlinear equity valuation using conic finance and its regulatory implications|first=Dilip B.|last=Madan|date=January 1, 2019|journal=Mathematics and Financial Economics|volume=13|issue=1|pages=31–65|via=Springer Link|doi=10.1007/s11579-018-0219-2|s2cid=255307573 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> More recently in 2016 and 2022, he co-authored with Wim Schoutens two books titled Applied Conic Finance and Nonlinear valuation and non-Gaussian risks in finance, which provided an overview of the newly established conic finance theory, including its theoretical framework and various applications.<ref name="auto"/>

===Options pricing===
Madan's options pricing research has focused on conducting empirical studies to test the performance of various option pricing models using real-world data.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.pm-research.com/content/iijderiv/25/1/10|title=Conic Option Pricing|first1=Dilip B.|last1=Madan|first2=Wim|last2=Schoutens|date=August 31, 2017|journal=The Journal of Derivatives|volume=25|issue=1|pages=10–36|via=www.pm-research.com|doi=10.3905/jod.2017.25.1.010|s2cid=157781092 |url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|url=http://www.jstor.org/stable/2962050|title=The Multinomial Option Pricing Model and its Brownian and Poisson Limits|author1=Madan, Dilip B.|author2=Milne, Frank|author3=Shefrin, Hersh|year=1989|journal=The Review of Financial Studies|volume=2|issue=2|pages=251–265|doi=10.1093/rfs/2.2.251 |jstor=2962050 |hdl=10419/67854|hdl-access=free}}</ref> While exploring the valuation of European call options employing the Vasicek-Gaussian [[stochastic process]], his research proposed an approach to approximate and determine the equilibrium change of measure in [[incomplete markets]], using log return mean, variance, and kurtosis.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1467-9965.1991.tb00018.x|title=Option Pricing With V. G. Martingale Components|first1=Dilip B.|last1=Madan|first2=Frank|last2=Milne|date=October 8, 1991|journal=Mathematical Finance|volume=1|issue=4|pages=39–55|via=CrossRef|doi=10.1111/j.1467-9965.1991.tb00018.x|s2cid=10650236 |hdl=10419/67879|hdl-access=free}}</ref> In a collaborative study with Robert A. Jarrow, he demonstrated the application of term-structure-associated financial instruments in formulating dynamic portfolio management tactics, specifically aimed at mitigating distinct systematic jump hazards inherent in asset returns.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1467-9965.1995.tb00070.x|first1=Robert|last1=Jarrow|first2=Dilip|last2=Madan|title=Option Pricing Using the Term Structure of Interest Rates to Hedge Systematic Discontinuities in Asset Returns |date=October 8, 1995|journal=Mathematical Finance|volume=5|issue=4|pages=311–336|via=CrossRef|doi=10.1111/j.1467-9965.1995.tb00070.x|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In his early works, he introduced the variance gamma process, a stochastic model for log stock price dynamics, highlighting its symmetric statistical density with some kurtosis and negatively skewed risk-neutral density with higher kurtosis.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://academic.oup.com/rof/article/2/1/79/1581894|title=The Variance Gamma Process and Option Pricing – Oxford Academic|journal=Review of Finance |date=January 1998 |volume=2 |issue=1 |pages=79–105 |doi=10.1023/A:1009703431535 |last1=Madan |first1=Dilip B. |last2=Carr |first2=Peter P. |last3=Chang |first3=Eric C. |url-access=subscription }}</ref> His study further proposed using Markov Chains and homogeneous Levy processes, specifically the variance gamma process, as a robust modeling approach for financial asset prices, thereby facilitating the computation of option and series prices.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1013816400834|title=Option Pricing Using Variance Gamma Markov Chains|first1=Mikhail|last1=Konikov|first2=Dilip B.|last2=Madan|date=January 1, 2002|journal=Review of Derivatives Research|volume=5|issue=1|pages=81–115|via=Springer Link|doi=10.1023/A:1013816400834|s2cid=152395231 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> His research work on pricing European options involved exploring self-similar risk-neutral processes and proposing two parameter stability-based models, highlighting their usefulness in studying the time variation of option prices.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1467-9965.2007.00293.x|first1=Peter|last1=Carr|first2=Hélyette|last2=Geman|first3=Dilip B.|last3=Madan|first4=Marc|last4=Yor|title=Self-Decomposability and Option Pricing |date=January 8, 2007|journal=Mathematical Finance|volume=17|issue=1|pages=31–57|via=CrossRef|doi=10.1111/j.1467-9965.2007.00293.x|s2cid=452963 |doi-access=free}}</ref> Concentrating his research on risk premia in options markets, he used the variance gamma model for density synthesis, revealing mean reversion and predictability in premia, with particular emphasis on short-term market crashes and long-term market rallies.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s10436-016-0273-9|title=Risk premia in option markets|first=Dilip B.|last=Madan|date=February 1, 2016|journal=Annals of Finance|volume=12|issue=1|pages=71–94|via=Springer Link|doi=10.1007/s10436-016-0273-9|s2cid=254196274 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> His recent work in 2021 has contributed to the understanding of risk-neutral densities and jump arrival tails by introducing theoretical examples and practical models based on quasi-infinitely divisible distributions.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/1350486X.2021.2007145|title=Risk Neutral Jump Arrival Rates Implied in Option Prices and Their Models|first1=Dilip B.|last1=Madan|first2=King|last2=Wang|date=May 4, 2021|journal=Applied Mathematical Finance|volume=28|issue=3|pages=201–235|via=CrossRef|doi=10.1080/1350486X.2021.2007145|s2cid=246344868 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

===Asset pricing===
Madan's contributions to asset pricing research have resulted in the development of asset pricing models.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s10436-014-0255-8|title=Asset pricing theory for two price economies|first=Dilip B.|last=Madan|date=February 1, 2015|journal=Annals of Finance|volume=11|issue=1|pages=1–35|via=Springer Link|doi=10.1007/s10436-014-0255-8|s2cid=254192304 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> His early research examined the minimum variance estimator to achieve a singular optimal power and provided approximations for estimating the scalar diffusion coefficient through the application of Ito calculus and Milstein methods.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1467-9965.1993.tb00080.x|title=Diffusion Coefficient Estimation and Asset Pricing When Risk Premia and Sensitivities Are Time Varying|first1=Marc|last1=Chesney|first2=Robert J.|last2=Elliott|first3=Dilip|last3=Madan|first4=Hailiang|last4=Yang|date=April 8, 1993|journal=Mathematical Finance|volume=3|issue=2|pages=85–99|via=CrossRef|doi=10.1111/j.1467-9965.1993.tb00080.x|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He also addressed the paradox posed by Artzner and Heath, offering a solution determining that completeness pertains to the topology of the cash flow space and is associated with the singular nature of the price functional in the topological dual space.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/1467-9965.00070|title=The Second Fundamental Theorem of Asset Pricing|first1=Robert A.|last1=Jarrow|first2=Xing|last2=Jin|first3=Dilip B.|last3=Madan|date=July 8, 1999|journal=Mathematical Finance|volume=9|issue=3|pages=255–273|via=CrossRef|doi=10.1111/1467-9965.00070|s2cid=120388047 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> In 2001, he proposed a modeling approach for asset price processes<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/2382067|title=Purely Discontinuous Asset Price Processes}}</ref> and illustrated that asset price dynamics are more suitably represented by pure jump processes, devoid of any continuous martingale component.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://ideas.repec.org//h/wsi/wschap/9789812810663_0004.html|title=Asset Prices Are Brownian Motion: Only In Business Time|first1=Helyette|last1=Geman|first2=Dilip B.|last2=Madan|first3=Marc|last3=Yor|date=August 8, 2001|journal=World Scientific Book Chapters|pages=103–146|via=ideas.repec.org}}</ref> In his analysis of equilibrium asset pricing, his work established that factor prices are influenced by exponentially tilted prices due to non-Gaussian factor risk exposures, which can be determined from the univariate probability distribution of the factor exposure.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/14697680600804437|title=Equilibrium asset pricing: with non-Gaussian factors and exponential utilities|first=Dilip B.|last=Madan|date=December 8, 2006|journal=Quantitative Finance|volume=6|issue=6|pages=455–463|via=CrossRef|doi=10.1080/14697680600804437|s2cid=154884070 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> Moreover, with Wim Schoutens, he co-developed a technique that uses historical data to establish upper and lower valuations, leading to enhanced risk evaluation in the stock market through the integration of risk attributes into required returns.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s10436-018-0328-1|title=Conic asset pricing and the costs of price fluctuations|first1=Dilip B.|last1=Madan|first2=Wim|last2=Schoutens|date=March 1, 2019|journal=Annals of Finance|volume=15|issue=1|pages=29–58|via=Springer Link|doi=10.1007/s10436-018-0328-1|s2cid=254197113 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>
